h1: The 6 Best Bed Frames with Storage of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bed Frames with Storage: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six storage bed frames, from hydraulic lift-ups to drawer beds and an 18 inch tall metal frame, with weight and budget advice.
summary: The Jocisland Queen lift-up is the best storage bed frame here, with a 1,000 lb capacity, hydraulic lift and a squeak-resistant mechanism. The Allewie and SHA CERLIN offer 800 lb lift-ups, the Lifezone is the drawer bed with charging, and the EMODA is the cheap, tall frame for bins. The HISOFT is the only King.
intro: Storage beds hide a trade-off that most listings bury. A lift-up frame gives you one huge cavity that you reach only by raising the whole mattress, while a drawer bed gives small compartments that open at a tug. If you will open the storage weekly, the access mechanism matters more than the stated volume, and it is worth knowing which style you will actually use.

We reviewed eight listings and ranked six on weight capacity, access style and clearance. Everything comes from the spec sheets, not from assembly in a workshop. The group splits four ways: hydraulic lift-ups, a drawer bed, a tall open-clearance frame and a single King, with capacities from 800 to 1,200 lb, and prices from the $50 to $100 bucket up to $200 to $500.

products.name: Jocisland Queen Linen Lift Up Storage Wingback
products.verdict: A 1,000 lb lift-up frame with a squeak-resistant mechanism.
products.description:
The Jocisland is a Queen hydraulic lift-up bed with a 1,000 lb capacity. The lift opens to 60 inches, the linen wingback headboard stands 52.1 inches tall, and the listing claims 40 percent more storage than a standard bed. Hydraulics hold the platform open so you can pull out bedding with both hands.

It ranks first because the capacity is among the highest here and the mechanism is labeled squeak-resistant. The Allewie below offers 800 lb for a similar bucket, and the Lifezone offers 800 lb with drawers. A 1,000 lb rating leaves room for a heavy mattress plus two sleepers.

It suits bulky bedding, luggage and off-season clothes. The caveat is the $200 to $500 price and the clearance: you need free space at the foot and sides to raise the platform, so nothing can sit against the bed.
products.idealFor: Owners with bulky bedding to store.

products.name: Allewie Queen Lift Up Hydraulic Storage
products.verdict: Gas hydraulic lift, solid wood slats and a linen finish.
products.description:
The Allewie is a Queen frame with an 800 lb capacity, gas hydraulic lift, solid wood slats and a linen-upholstered wingback headboard with channel design, in the $200 to $500 bucket. Gas struts hold the platform up and carry its weight, so lifting is a light pull rather than a heave. Solid wood slats support the mattress evenly.

It ranks second because the capacity trails the Jocisland's 1,000 lb, though the feature set is similar. It beats the SHA CERLIN by listing solid wood slats without plastic buckles in the bullets, and it costs the same bracket. The lower weight rating is the main reason it sits behind.

Good for a classic upholstered look. The caveat is that lower rating: two heavier sleepers plus a thick hybrid mattress eat into 800 lb.
products.idealFor: Buyers who like a classic upholstered look.

products.name: SHA CERLIN Queen Lift Up Wingback Storage
products.verdict: Hydraulic lift platform that needs no box spring.
products.description:
The SHA CERLIN is a Queen frame with an 800 lb capacity and a hydraulic lift platform. It has solid wood slats with plastic buckles, a wingback headboard with horizontal channels, and needs no box spring. The platform replaces the box spring entirely, which can cut cost and height if you are swapping from an older bed.

It ranks third because it matches the Allewie on capacity and bucket but gives fewer extras. Plastic buckles hold the slats in place, and plastic is the part most likely to wear. Next to the Jocisland, it gives up 200 lb of capacity.

Suits those who want a simple lift in an upholstered frame. The caveat is the plastic buckles on the slats, which can crack under repeated lifting, so check them after assembly.
products.idealFor: People replacing an old box-spring bed.

products.name: Lifezone Queen 4 Drawers + LED + Charging
products.verdict: Four sliding drawers and a tiered headboard with charging.
products.description:
The Lifezone is a Queen bed rated for 800 lb in the $100 to $200 bucket. It pairs four sliding drawers with a two-tier headboard and two AC outlets, plus USB and Type-C charging. Lighting is RGB and can be driven from an app or a remote, and eleven metal rods support the frame.

It ranks fourth because drawers give easier access than lifting a mattress, but total volume is smaller than a lift-up cavity. It is also a bracket cheaper than the lift-up frames above, with charging built in, which none of them offer. The metal rods suggest a sturdy base for the drawers.

Best for everyday access to socks, clothes and chargers. The caveat is floor space: drawers need clearance in front to slide, and they cannot hold bulky items like comforters or suitcases.
products.idealFor: Daily access to socks and clothing.
products.skipIf: You need to store bulky items.

products.name: EMODA Queen 18 Inch Tall Metal Storage
products.verdict: The tallest under-bed clearance here, at the lowest price.
products.description:
The EMODA is a metal Queen frame with 18 inches of under-bed clearance, a 1,200 lb capacity, nine reinforced legs and tool-free assembly in about 20 minutes, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Eighteen inches is the tallest clearance in the guide, tall enough for large bins, suitcases and even a rolling drawer.

It ranks fifth because it offers no built-in drawers, so you supply the bins, but it is the cheapest of the six and has the highest weight rating. Against the Lifezone and the hydraulic beds, it gives open storage you can shape yourself. It has DIY headboard holes, but no headboard comes with it.

Ideal for renters who own storage bins. The caveat is looks and effort: the frame is plain, the headboard is extra, and you have to bend and pull to reach what is stored beneath.

products.name: HISOFT King Hydraulic Lift + Metal Slats + Linen
products.verdict: King size lift-up with full metal slats and noise foam.
products.description:
The HISOFT is a King frame with a 1,000 lb capacity, a pair of gas lifts rated for 160 lbs of force, slats made entirely of metal, EVA foam padding at every joint against noise, and a tufted linen wingback headboard, in the $200 to $500 bucket. Dual gas lifts share the load across a wide King platform.

It ranks last only because King size suits fewer rooms, though it is the only one here at that size. Foam at the joints addresses the squeak that metal slats can produce, and metal slats hold their shape under load better than wood. Against the Jocisland, it matches the 1,000 lb capacity but adds size.

Choose it for a large bedroom with space to lift. The caveat is its size: a King lift-up needs clear room at the foot and sides, and the frame is heavy to assemble.
products.idealFor: Large bedrooms needing King size storage.

whatMatters.detail: Lift-up frames raise the whole platform to reveal one big cavity, while drawers slide out in sections. Lift-ups hold bulkier items but need space above and beside the bed to open. Drawers suit frequent use. Check the listing for the mechanism name, and picture how you will reach what is stored when the room is cramped and the mattress is made.

Weight capacity is the maximum load the frame supports, such as 800 or 1,000 lb. It includes the mattress and sleepers. A heavy hybrid mattress can consume a quarter of the rating. Look for the pounds figure in the specs, and add the mattress, the sleepers and a margin for children or pets who join the bed.

Clearance is the gap between floor and slats, like the EMODA's 18 inches. It decides whether bins, suitcases and rolling drawers fit. Look for the inch figure in the specs, and compare it with your tallest bin. Hydraulic beds do not state clearance because the storage is a cavity, so check the listed lift height and interior depth instead.

Queen and King frames need very different room space. Measure the room including walkways, and remember that a lift-up needs extra clearance to open. Listings state the size in the title. The HISOFT is the only King here. A large frame also affects how furniture and doors fit around the bed.

Squeaks come from slat joints, hinges and lifts. Foam strips or noise padding help. The Jocisland is labeled squeak-resistant, a claim worth confirming, and the HISOFT adds EVA foam at every joint. Look for terms like noise foam or squeak-resistant, and plan to tighten bolts after the first month of use, because wood and metal settle.

faq.q: Do these need a box spring?
faq.a: The SHA CERLIN says no box spring needed. Check each listing for others, because a lift-up with slats usually replaces the box spring, while the EMODA metal frame also supports the mattress directly, so confirm slat spacing.

Ignoring lift clearance. A lift-up bed needs room above and beside it to open fully, so a nightstand or wall can block the platform. Measure first, with the lift fully open and the headboard in place.

faq.q: Is lift-up worth it over drawers?
faq.a: For bulky items, yes. The Jocisland holds large bedding and luggage. For daily clothes, the Lifezone drawers are easier because you do not have to raise the whole mattress.

The EMODA lists about 20 minutes with no tools. Others vary, and the hydraulic beds are heavier, so allow help and time, and clear the floor first. Check each listing for assembly notes and parts count before you start.
Tighten bolts periodically. The HISOFT adds EVA foam at every joint, and the Jocisland is labeled squeak-resistant. Retighten hardware after the first few weeks of use, and again each season.

Check the slat spacing and the weight rating against your mattress, and read the mattress maker's support rules. Heavy hybrids and thick memory foam need solid support, like the wood slats on the Allewie or the metal slats on the HISOFT.

finalTake: Buy the Jocisland if you want a lift-up bed for bulky bedding and luggage. Choose the Lifezone for daily access to clothes, and the EMODA when you already own bins and want the lowest price. King-size bedrooms should look at the HISOFT, the only frame here at that size.
